subject.title: [Feature]: Expose before_tool_call/after_tool_call in internal hooks system

question: Should managed HOOK.md hooks become an enforceable tool-call policy surface, or should before_tool_call/after_tool_call remain typed-plugin-only with validation and diagnostics for unsupported HOOK.md events?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing managed hooks before tool execution changes OpenClaw's security boundary and plugin API contract; automation cannot choose trust, ordering, timeout, failure, and compatibility semantics safely.

options.title: Design managed tool-call hooks
options.body: Add typed managed/internal before and after tool-call events that compose with trusted policies and plugin hooks across all tool execution surfaces, with docs and focused regression coverage.

options.title: Keep tool policy plugin-only
options.body: Reject or warn on before_tool_call and after_tool_call in HOOK.md metadata and point users to typed plugin hooks or ClawHub-packaged code plugins for enforceable policy.

options.title: Expose telemetry only
options.body: Add non-blocking after-call observation for managed hooks while keeping pre-tool blocking and parameter rewrites in the typed plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Design managed tool-call hooks
recommendation.body: Add typed managed/internal before and after tool-call events that compose with trusted policies and plugin hooks across all tool execution surfaces, with docs and focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the original internal hook surface and already provided maintainer signal on this canonical tracker.
